ref_extractions.title: Human infant EEG recordings for 200 object images presented in rapid visual streams
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the primary data descriptor paper that explicitly describes and releases the openneuro_ds005106 dataset. It provides full details of 42 infant participants, 200 object images in RSVP paradigm at 5Hz, and includes technical validation with RSA decoding showing category-level representations are decodable.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: Stimulus-triggered epochs; each of 200 objects presented at 5Hz with 100ms on/100ms off; at least 3 repetitions per object per participant
ref_extractions.label_mapping: Three levels: object ID (50), category (10: mammal/fruit/tool/etc.), superordinate (2: animate/inanimate)
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Superordinate (animate/inanimate) is primary label; mid-level categories and individual object IDs also available
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Technical validation section shows successful category-level decoding using RSA and MVPA, demonstrating discriminable neural responses to object categories in infants >6 months

ref_extractions.title: Perceptual similarity of visual patterns predicts dynamic neural activation patterns measured with MEG
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This MEG study uses abstract Gabor patch stimuli, not the 200 object images from the infant EEG dataset. The experimental paradigm and stimuli are entirely different. It investigates perceptual similarity judgments, not infant object recognition.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses abstract visual patterns (Gabor patches) with adult participants in MEG; no connection to the infant EEG dataset or RSVP object presentation paradigm

ref_extractions.title: The representational dynamics of visual objects in rapid serial visual processing streams

tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Superordinate Object Category Classification (Animate vs Inanimate)

**Task Type**: Classification | **Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5 | **Label Route**: misc | **Meta Level**: super

**Epoch Parameters**:
| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| tmin | -0.2 s | Pre-stimulus baseline |
| tmax | 0.8 s | Captures N200/N400 responses |
| Event IDs | 1–200 | 200 distinct object IDs |

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| 1–200 (selected subset) | 0 | Inanimate object |
| 1–200 (selected subset) | 1 | Animate object |

**Label Source**: Hierarchical label mapping from object IDs to superordinate category (animate/inanimate). Code -1 (baseline/inter-stimulus) excluded.

**Evidence** (DOI): https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04744-z | https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/dzrkq

**Kernel Notes**: Event codes 1–200 map to 200 distinct object images organized into binary superordinate categories. Technical validation in the original publication demonstrates successful category-level decoding using RSA and MVPA, showing discriminable neural responses to animate vs. inanimate objects in infants >6 months. Primary developmental label for infant object cognition research.

---

### Classical Task 2: Mid-Level Category Classification (10-Category)

**Task Type**: Classification | **Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5 | **Label Route**: misc | **Meta Level**: raw

**Epoch Parameters**:
| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| tmin | -0.2 s | Pre-stimulus baseline |
| tmax | 0.8 s | Post-stimulus response window |
| Event IDs | 1–200 | Object presentation events |

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| 1–200 | 0–9 | 10 mid-level categories (mammal, fruit, tool, etc.) |

**Label Source**: Hierarchical label mapping from 200 object IDs to 10 mid-level semantic categories. Code -1 excluded.

**Evidence** (DOI): https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04744-z | https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/dzrkq

**Kernel Notes**: Objects are grouped into 10 semantic categories (e.g., mammal, fruit, tool, vehicle, etc.). The paper's technical validation section explicitly demonstrates category-level decoding, confirming that infant EEG contains distinguishable representations for these mid-level categories at 5Hz RSVP presentation rates.

---

### Potential Task 1: Individual Object Identity Decoding (200-Class)

**Task Type**: Classification | **Epoch Method**: epoch_by_event_hdf5 | **Label Route**: event | **Meta Level**: raw

**Epoch Parameters**:
| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| tmin | -0.2 s | Pre-stimulus baseline |
| tmax | 0.8 s | Per-object neural response |
| Event IDs | 1–200 | Each code = unique object |

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| 1 | 1 | Object ID 1 |
| 2 | 2 | Object ID 2 |
| ... | ... | ... |
| 200 | 200 | Object ID 200 |

**Label Source**: Event code itself serves as object identity label. Code -1 excluded.


**Evidence** (DOI): None (plausible from paradigm; each event ID uniquely maps to one of 200 stimuli)

**Kernel Notes**: With ~217–220 epochs per object ID across 42 subjects (~5 presentations per object per subject), there is sufficient data for within-subject decoding of individual object identities. However, the reference paper focuses on category-level analysis rather than individual object identity, making this a potential rather than classical task. High-dimensional 200-class classification is challenging in infant EEG due to lower signal-to-noise ratio.


---

### Normal Task 1: Inter-Stimulus Baseline Characterization

**Task Type**: Characterization | **Epoch Method**: epoch_by_long_event_hdf5 | **Label Route**: stim | **Meta Level**: raw


**Epoch Parameters**:
| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| tmin | 0.0 s | From baseline onset |
| tmax | 2.0 s | Capture inter-stream baseline |
| Event ID | -1 | Baseline/inter-stimulus marker |

**Target Definition**:
| Event | y | Meaning |
|-------|---|---------|
| -1 | 0 | Inter-stimulus baseline period |

**Label Source**: Code -1 marks baseline periods between RSVP streams.

**Evidence** (DOI): None (kernel-inferred; -1 appears 43,105 times across dataset)

**Kernel Notes**: Event -1 appears 43,105 times, representing inter-stimulus/baseline periods in the RSVP paradigm. Long epochs on these markers are useful for artifact detection, baseline correction, and characterizing resting-state or transitional EEG activity between rapid visual streams in infant data with high artifact rates.
